correctness.rationale: For total Roman {2} domination on B_m (m≥2 shared-edge four-cycles), labels f∈{0,1,2}; a zero needs open-neighborhood label sum≥2, and each positive vertex needs a positive neighbor. The spine labeling (2,2) and all-zero pages always has weight four. With fixed spine (a,b), minimum page sums are 0 for (2,2) uniquely at (0,0), 2 for (0,0), and 1 for every other spine pair, subject to later totality checks. When m≥4 those bounds already exclude weight ≤4 off the spine; when m=3 the only remaining a+b=1 patterns produce isolated page-positive vertices. Therefore m≥3 has the unique spine optimum. For m=2, totality eliminates spurious page patterns and yields precisely six minimizers: spine(2,2), all page ones/spine zero, and four (1,1) spine variants, one positive page vertex on each page. Fresh exhaustive enumeration gives (m,min,count)=(2,4,6),(3,4,1),(4,4,1). The case-based proof covers all m≥2; m=1=C4 has optimum 3 and is excluded.
